commands.review_summary:
Adds cron CLI channel-type validation, help text updates, and regression tests for `cron add/edit --channel` and `cron edit --failure-alert-channel`.

PR surface: Source +76, Tests +217. Total +293 across 5 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level. Current main stores `--channel` and `--failure-alert-channel` values without validating channel type, and the PR diff shows the proposed validator can reject external plugin IDs because the cron CLI does not load plugins.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow repair can make the validator preserve external channel plugin compatibility while keeping the intended early CLI error for channel IDs passed as channel types.

target.title: fix(cron-cli): validate cron --channel against known channel types
target.body:
Fixes #102596

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw cron add` and `openclaw cron edit` take a `--channel <x>` flag (and `cron edit` a `--failure-alert-channel <x>` flag). These name the delivery **channel plugin TYPE** (`last | slack | telegram | discord | ...`), not a channel id - the channel **id** belongs in `--to` / `--failure-alert-to`.

Both flags accepted any string and stored it unvalidated. Because Slack itself labels an id like `C0BFYTH0BSP` a "channel ID", users naturally pass it to `--channel`. The job is written happily, then delivery fails much later at **runtime** with `OutboundDeliveryError: channel_not_found` and no hint about the real mistake. The flag help even rendered a misleading `last|<channel-id>` placeholder, nudging users toward passing an id.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fail fast with a clear, actionable error at add/edit time instead of a confusing runtime delivery failure, and stop the help text from steering users wrong.

Key subtlety: the thin `cron` CLI client registers plugin *commands* but never loads channel plugin *runtimes*, so `listChannelPlugins()` (the source `getCronChannelOptions()` used) is empty in that process - validating against it alone would silently never fire. The known-type set is therefore sourced from the generated bundled channel catalog (`CHANNEL_IDS` / `normalizeChatChannelId` in `src/channels/ids.ts`), which is available synchronously without any plugin runtime, plus any loaded channel plugins so external/in-process contexts still extend the set. This keeps `getCronChannelOptions()` and validation on one source of truth so they cannot drift.

Changes (all in `src/cli/cron-cli/`):
- `shared.ts` - new `assertKnownCronChannelType()` and a shared `listKnownCronChannelTypes()` (bundled catalog + loaded plugins + `last`); `getCronChannelOptions()` now renders real channel types instead of `last|<channel-id>`.
- `register.cron-add.ts` - validate `--channel` (only when user-supplied, not the `last` default).
- `register.cron-edit.ts` - validate `--channel` and `--failure-alert-channel`.
- Flag help updated to read as a channel TYPE and point the id at `--to` / `--failure-alert-to`.

Accepts bundled types (case-insensitively, incl. aliases) and loaded external plugin ids; rejects channel ids like `C0BFYTH0BSP`. `--clear-channel` / omitting the flag are unaffected.

## User Impact

`openclaw cron add`/`edit` now reject a channel id passed to a channel-type flag with a clear hint, before the job is written:

```
$ openclaw cron edit <job> --failure-alert-channel BOGUS
Error: Unknown channel type "BOGUS" for --failure-alert-channel. Valid: last|...|slack|telegram|... .
Did you mean --failure-alert-to <channel-id>? A channel id (e.g. a Slack "C0..." id) goes in
--failure-alert-to, not --failure-alert-channel.
```

Valid types (`--channel slack`, aliases, `last`, loaded plugin ids) and omitting the flag behave exactly as before. No config/schema/protocol changes.

## Evidence

- New tests `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-channel-validation.test.ts` (9 cases): `add`/`edit --channel <id>` and `edit --failure-alert-channel <id>` are rejected at parse/edit time with the hint and no gateway call; a valid type (`slack`), a case-insensitive match (`Slack`), a loaded external plugin id (`acme`), and omitting the flag all still work. Updated `shared.test.ts` for the new `getCronChannelOptions()` source.
- `pnpm test src/cli/cron-cli` - green (11 + 74 tests across configs).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:import-cycles`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm format:check`, `oxlint` on changed files - all green.
- Manual CLI (real built binary):
  - `cron edit <job> --failure-alert-channel BOGUS` -> edit-time `Unknown channel type` error, no job written.
  - `cron add "T" --every 10m --message hi --agent a1 --announce --channel C0BFYTH0BSP` -> rejected with `--to` hint.
  - `cron edit <job> --channel slack` -> passes validation, proceeds to the gateway call (creds prompt), confirming valid types are unaffected.
  - `cron edit --help` now lists real channel types for `--channel <type>` / `--failure-alert-channel <type>`.
